title: FathomGrid Integration Discovery — gateway / VPC tradeoffs
summary: Initial integration discovery. FathomGrid is evaluating Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private for a customer-facing conversational assistant. Main concerns: VPC/private control, rate limits/tenant quotas, gateway/proxy pattern vs sidecar, LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors, observability hooks into Datadog, and SOC2/KMS requirements. Agreed next steps: send security pack + network diagram, proposal for a 6-week POC with Dedicated capacity + sandbox VPC, and schedule an architecture deep dive with SREs next week.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private decision criteria
Rate limiting, tenant quotas and burst handling
Observability hooks and tracing to Datadog
Security: SSO, KMS, audit logs, data residency

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-29 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~61 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Oliver Park (CTO, FathomGrid), Sofia Rahman (Platform Eng), Amir Khan (SRE), Tess Nguyen (Security)

Auto-generated summary: discussed integration patterns and risk areas.

[00:00:05] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, really appreciate it. Quick intro from our side, I'm Maya, I'm the AE working with platform teams, um Daniel and Priya are our SEs who will walk through technical bits.
[00:00:18] Oliver Park: Hi Maya, hi team. Oliver here. We have a short agenda: figure out whether hosted/dedicated/private makes sense, and how we actually wire it into our gateway.
[00:00:27] Daniel Ortiz: Cool, thanks. Quick check — is the goal to put Redwood behind your existing gateway proxy, or are you open to a sidecar approach?
[00:00:34] Sofia Rahman: We prefer behind the gateway, ideally. We run an Envoy edge and then our internal gateway, we don't want to re-architect for sidecars if we can avoid it.
[00:00:42] Amir Khan: Yeah, also need to understand token accounting and quotas per tenant. We have multi-tenant customers and we need to cap spend and burst.
[00:00:49] Maya Chen: Totally, that's a common pattern. We support gateway/proxy integration — many customers do that for routing to hosted or to a VPC endpoint for private. There's a few tradeoffs: latency, connection churn, and how you handle KV caching and conversational context.
[00:01:05] Priya Nair: To add, if you put Redwood behind a gateway you can still do per-tenant routing — we can route headers or tokens to different model variants or dedicated pools.
[00:01:12] Tess Nguyen: Security question: we need to see KMS integrations and proof of encryption at rest and in transit, plus audit log retention for at least 1 year. Do you have SOC2 stuff?
[00:01:21] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll send the SOC2 report and our encryption docs. We support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations in the Private offering; Dedicated also has options.
[00:01:30] Oliver Park: For latency, our SLA target is p95 < 800ms for short chat turns. Can hosted meet that, or do we need Dedicated?
[00:01:40] Daniel Ortiz: Hosted often hits that for smaller models and lower concurrency but it depends on payload size. For predictable p95 under heavy concurrency, Dedicated pools are safer — you can reserve GPUs and avoid noisy neighbor effects. Also want to highlight batching: we can do continuous batching but you tune based on your latency SLOs.
[00:01:58] Sofia Rahman: How does batching affect token billing? We don't want spikes on cost from hidden batching behavior.
[00:02:04] Priya Nair: Good Q — batching reduces per-token compute cost by combining requests, so usually handles cost better. We surface token-level and compute-level breakdown in the Console so you can see when batching savings occur. There's also an explicit batching config so you can set max delay to control latency/cost tradeoff.
[00:02:19] Amir Khan: About SDKs — we use LangChain and LlamaIndex in several services. How mature are your adapters?
[00:02:25] Daniel Ortiz: We have official SDKs and first-class connectors for LangChain and LlamaIndex. Most customers use the SDK server-side and wire into LangChain chains. There are a few gotchas around streaming and tool calls, especially if you route through a gateway proxy that strips chunked responses — you'd want to ensure the proxy supports streaming APIs.
[00:02:45] Oliver Park: Ah that might be a blocker. Our current gateway terminates HTTP/1.1 and we sometimes lose stream. What's the workaround?
[00:02:52] Maya Chen: Two options: make the gateway pass through chunked responses, or do a websocket passthrough to Redwood's streaming endpoint. For POC we usually test both and prefer passthrough if you want minimal changes.
[00:03:06] Sofia Rahman: Observability — we run Datadog and expect traces and logs. Can Redwood emit spans and token-level traces to external APM?
[00:03:13] Priya Nair: Yes, we have tracing hooks and can export trace IDs and sampling metadata. You can plug our tracing to Datadog via our sidecar or via headers that we forward in hosted. There's also per-route dashboards in the Console and a trace link back to the raw request in our tracing UI.
[00:03:29] Amir Khan: Do you include prompt inputs in logs? We need to redact PII and control retention.
[00:03:36] Daniel Ortiz: By default we mask sensitive fields and redact based on rules; for Private deployments you can configure retention and full control over logging. Hosted allows configurable retention windows, and we support redaction rules and tokenization hooks.
[00:03:49] Oliver Park: Anything around tenant quotas? We need per-customer quotas and bursting behavior — e.g., customer A can burst to 2x for short periods but we need to cap monthly tokens.
[00:03:58] Maya Chen: We have tenant-level quotas and throttles, plus burst buckets. Our rate-limiter supports token bucket semantics and you can configure per-route and per-API-key limits. Also we expose quota usage in near real-time in the Console and via API.
[00:04:13] Sofia Rahman: How about emergencies — fail open/closed behavior? We want graceful degradation: fall back to smaller model or cached responses.
[00:04:20] Daniel Ortiz: Exactly — you can set fallbacks: route to a cheaper/quantized model, or serve cached replies from prefix/KV cache. We also support automatic fallback policies by latency or error thresholds.
[00:04:32] Tess Nguyen: On compliance: can we run Redwood Private in our VPC or on-prem? We have data residency constraints for EU customers.
[00:04:40] Maya Chen: Yes: Redwood Private can be deployed into your VPC with a private control plane; we also have an on-prem package for air-gapped environments. For EU residency we can restrict data region and use customer-managed keys.
[00:04:52] Oliver Park: Cost — from a procurement lens, what's the delta between hosted and Dedicated? We're trying to make the case to finance.
[00:04:59] Maya Chen: Hosted is pay-as-you-go (per-token/per-embedding), Dedicated is reserved capacity with a monthly commit. Typically Dedicated lowers per-token cost at scale but requires a commit. For a POC we can propose a short-term Dedicated estimate or a hosted trial with committed burst.
[00:05:12] Sofia Rahman: For the POC we want to hit a realistic traffic pattern: 100k tokens/day, bursts to 500k/day during promotions. Can you accommodate?
[00:05:21] Daniel Ortiz: Yes, that profile is typical. We'll size a pool with burst headroom; we also recommend enabling prefix caching for repeated prompts to lower token consumption.
[00:05:30] Amir Khan: One technical nuance: we use a gateway that mutates some headers and injects X-User-ID at the edge. We need to ensure full request fidelity so token attribution maps to tenant.
[00:05:40] Priya Nair: Pass-through headers are supported. For tenant attribution it's best to use API keys per tenant or include a signed header that we validate. We'll share examples for how customers do this with Envoy and Istio.
[00:05:51] Oliver Park: About SDKs again — we have Python microservices and some Go. Do you have first-class Go support?
[00:05:58] Daniel Ortiz: SDKs for Python, Node and Go are available; Go SDK is stable but we can share some example repos for LangChain-like patterns in Go.
[00:06:07] Maya Chen: Ok let's walk through an example flow — Sophia, is it okay if we sketch a quick diagram?
[00:06:12] Sofia Rahman: Sure. (brief pause) So request comes in to Envoy, goes to our gateway, gateway routes to internal service which calls Redwood. We currently do JWT auth.
[00:06:23] Daniel Ortiz: In that pattern we recommend creating an internal service that mints per-tenant API keys for Redwood and enforces quota. Alternatively you can route all calls through a single Redwood account and pass tenant info in headers and have Redwood enforce quotas per header; both approaches have pros and cons for billing visibility.
[00:06:40] Amir Khan: We need billing visibility per tenant; finance will ask for a clean mapping.
[00:06:44] Maya Chen: For billing clarity, many customers use dedicated API keys per tenant, then consolidate billing on your side. Redwood can also emit per-tenant usage logs to your billing pipeline.
[00:06:55] Oliver Park: We have a few proof-of-concept security hurdles: network egress approvals and SOC docs. Tess will own the security checklist.
[00:07:02] Tess Nguyen: Yup. I'll need the SOC2, encryption, and an architecture diagram showing egress flows and IP ranges. Also curious about MFA for console and SSO.
[00:07:11] Maya Chen: We'll include SSO/SAML docs and how RBAC maps to console roles. We'll also send allowed IP ranges and VPC peering options.
[00:07:18] Sofia Rahman: Can we get a short sketch of the integration timeline? From our side, we can commit to a 6-week POC if Redwood provides a test Dedicated pool and we get initial security signoff.
[00:07:27] Daniel Ortiz: That sounds reasonable. Week 1: network + security review and provisioning. Weeks 2–4: integration and telemetry hookup. Weeks 5–6: workload ramp and evaluation. We'll prepare a POC doc.
[00:07:39] Oliver Park: Any blockers on your side to start?
[00:07:42] Maya Chen: Need your traffic profile, network diagram, and security point-of-contact. We'll turn around the security pack within a few business days.
[00:07:50] Priya Nair: One more note — on streaming and LangChain tool calls, if you instrument tool calls that trigger external APIs, ensure the gateway preserves chunked responses or else streaming will degrade. Some customers do a small proxy tweak for a few endpoints.
[00:08:05] Amir Khan: Noted.
[00:08:08] (Conversation continues with Q&A and clarifications; transcript below contains selected excerpts)

[00:30:12] Sofia Rahman: Quick nit: when you mention KV cache, are you talking about prefix caching in the runtime or an external cache?
[00:30:18] Daniel Ortiz: Runtime prefix/KV cache; it's an in-memory cache that reduces tokens for repeated contexts. It can be shared across requests in a Dedicated pool but with Private you can also plug in external cache backends to persist state.
[00:30:30] Oliver Park: For Private VPC, what's the control plane model? Do you still call Redwood-managed control plane?
[00:30:37] Maya Chen: Private offers a customer-managed control plane option where the control plane runs in your VPC with a thin agent that connects to Redwood for updates. For strict air-gap we have an on-prem bundle.
[00:30:47] Tess Nguyen: How do you handle patching and runtime updates in Private?
[00:30:50] Priya Nair: We provide signed release artifacts and a patching playbook. For managed Private in VPC we can orchestrate upgrades under a change window; for on-prem you run the agent and apply signed packages.
[00:30:59] Oliver Park: Anything else on quotas?
[00:31:03] Daniel Ortiz: We'll send sample rate limiter configs. You can do both token-level and request-level controls. There's also burst capacity policies so a tenant can consume extra for short windows then be throttled back.
[00:31:12] Maya Chen: Ok we're almost at time — quick recap and next steps.
[00:31:20] Maya Chen: Recap: Redwood supports gateway/proxy integration, SDKs with LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors, tenant quotas, tracing to Datadog, and Private deployments into VPCs with KMS. You asked for security pack, POC plan, network diagram, and traffic profile.
[00:31:35] Oliver Park: Sounds good. Tess will coordinate the security review and Sofia will send traffic numbers.
[00:31:40] Amir Khan: We'll also want a short demo of streaming through our gateway; maybe do that in the deep-dive.
[00:31:46] Maya Chen: Great — we'll schedule the SRE deep dive for next week, send the security docs and a draft POC proposal. Anything else?
[00:31:53] Sofia Rahman: No, that's it. Thanks.
[00:31:55] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone.

End of transcript (selected). Some transcription errors present: e.g., 'KV cash' in earlier auto notes, small misattributions.
